Audit logging and hooks

Source: vignettes/audit-logging.Rmd
audit-logging.Rmd

Overview

An audit log records login attempts, token operations and session changes, helping explain a failed sign-in or why a session ended.

shinyOAuth sends each event to an R function called a hook. Your hook decides where to write it: the console for local testing, or your application’s logging service in a deployment. For timings and monitoring dashboards, see OpenTelemetry.

Receiving audit events

Put this near the top of app.R, before creating the provider and client:

options(shinyOAuth.audit_hook = function(event) {
  cat(sprintf("[shinyOAuth] %s | %s\n", event[["type"]], event[["trace_id"]]))
  str(event)
})

Run the app and sign in. Events such as audit_redirect_issued and audit_login_success describe the steps taken. The trace_id connects events from the same login attempt, including failures spanning several steps. Several error events can describe one failed login.

The hook runs as part of the recorded operation, so a slow logging service can delay login. options(shinyOAuth.audit_hook = NULL) disables the hook.

Authentication outcomes

Start with audit_authenticated_changed for the module’s authentication state and audit_session_cleared for why a session ended. A successful token exchange is an intermediate step; later identity checks can still reject the login.

Event structure

Audit events have type, trace_id, and a timestamp from Sys.time(), plus fields specific to the operation. The hook also receives error events such as error, http_error, and transport_error; their fields are listed in the catalog. Fields depend on the event and available context.

When a Shiny session is available, shiny_session contains:

  • session_token_digest: a protected identifier for correlating the session.
  • is_async and process_id: whether work ran in a background worker and which R process emitted the event. Async context also includes main_process_id.
  • http: a summary with request method, host, and scheme by default.

The session context is a JSON-friendly list suitable for jsonlite::toJSON(); the raw Shiny session[["request"]] object is not included. If shinyOAuth.audit_include_raw_session_token = TRUE, the raw session token is available as shiny_session[["token"]] in native hook events.

Fields ending in _digest allow matching without recording the original token or identifier. The package’s trace_id is separate from OpenTelemetry trace/span IDs; OTel exports it as shinyoauth.trace_id.

HTTP context and redaction

The default HTTP summary omits raw session tokens, request paths, query strings, headers and client addresses.

To omit HTTP context entirely:

options(shinyOAuth.audit_include_http = FALSE)

shinyOAuth.telemetry_path_scrubber supplies route labels for logs, for example replacing /users/123 with /users/:id. Paths remain omitted when no scrubber is configured.

Audit events from asynchronous workers

With async = TRUE, the hook also runs in background R processes. Shared logging needs a service supporting several writers and connections opened within each process. A global list collects only the current process’s events.

Digest keys across R processes

Digest fields let you match events without logging the original identifier. The default key lasts for one R process and its async workers. If you need to match records across app processes or restarts, load the same secret key in each:

audit_digest_key <- Sys.getenv("AUDIT_DIGEST_KEY", unset = NA_character_)
if (is.na(audit_digest_key) || !nzchar(audit_digest_key)) {
  stop("AUDIT_DIGEST_KEY must be configured before the app starts")
}
options(shinyOAuth.audit_digest_key = audit_digest_key)

The shared key contains at least 32 cryptographically random bytes and provides log correlation across processes, independently of login-state keys.

Event catalog

Event names identify the operation below. trace_id links records from one attempt; phase, reason, status and error_class add context when available. audit_login_success records completion of the login checks.

Login and callbacks

Name What it tells you
audit_redirect_issued The authorization URL is ready.
audit_callback_received Encrypted-state validation passed; later checks can still fail.
audit_callback_query_rejected Callback parameters are malformed or too large.
audit_callback_routing_rejected The callback could not be assigned to a configured client.
audit_callback_iss_missing The callback omitted a required provider identifier.
audit_callback_iss_mismatch The provider identifier does not match the expected issuer.
audit_callback_iss_validation_failed Another issuer check failed.
audit_callback_validation_success State, browser binding and single-use checks passed.
audit_callback_validation_failed A callback check failed; inspect phase and error_class.
audit_state_parse_failure Login state could not be decoded or validated.
audit_state_store_lookup_failed The pending login record could not be read.
audit_state_store_removal_failed The pending record could not be consumed safely.
audit_error_state_consumed State from a provider error response was consumed; other checks can still fail.
audit_error_state_consumption_failed State from a provider error response could not be consumed.
audit_browser_cookie_error Browser cookie setup failed or Web Crypto is unavailable.
audit_invalid_browser_token The browser sent an invalid binding token; the module requests a replacement.
audit_login_success Callback handling completed its configured checks.
audit_login_failed Login failed during callback handling.

Tokens and profiles

Name What it tells you
audit_token_exchange An authorization code was exchanged for tokens.
audit_token_exchange_error Token exchange failed.
audit_token_refresh The access token was refreshed.
audit_token_introspection A token-activity check finished; inspect active and status.
audit_token_revocation A revocation attempt finished, or was unsupported or missing a token.
audit_userinfo Profile retrieval or validation finished; status describes the result.

Sessions and saved connections

Name What it tells you
audit_session_started The authentication module started for a Shiny session.
audit_authenticated_changed The module authentication state changed.
audit_logout The module received a logout request.
audit_session_cleared Local login state was cleared; reason explains why.
audit_refresh_failed_but_kept_session Refresh failed, but indefinite_session = TRUE retained local login state.
audit_connection_disconnected One retained connection was removed locally.
audit_connections_disconnected A bulk local removal finished, including an empty batch.
audit_session_ended The Shiny session ended.
audit_session_ended_revoke Session end triggered configured token-revocation cleanup.

Error records

Name What it tells you
error The package raised an R error; inspect the error class and available context.
http_error A provider returned an unsuccessful HTTP status.
transport_error A request failed before a response arrived, for example after a timeout.

Disconnect events confirm local removal even if remote revocation fails. The per-connection remote_refresh_outcome and remote_access_outcome describe the remote attempts; an accepted request does not prove the provider recognized the token. Ending a Shiny session leaves browser- and account-retained connections in place.

For audit_userinfo, status distinguishes successful parsing from invalid JSON, missing identity fields, and signature or claim failures. HTTP error records can also include status and structured oauth_error fields. Free-form provider messages are subject to the package’s diagnostic redaction policy.

For DPoP nonce handling and mTLS endpoint selection, inspect the related OpenTelemetry spans.
